project.researchNotes:
Full visitor audit completed 2026-08-07. Statutory records come from the locally bundled Historic England NHLE download. The public planner contains only researched, named places inside the active visitor boundary. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-08: 260 of 294 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown. Peterborough See and Eat coverage was expanded on 2026-08-08 after a complete boundary-aware bundled-data and current OSM discrepancy sweep; only researched visitor choices were published. Peterborough See and practical coverage was expanded on 2026-08-08 after a complete boundary-aware bundled-data and current OSM discrepancy sweep. Eat was refined to daytime lunch, coffee, cake and afternoon-tea choices only; dinner-led restaurants and drink-led pubs were excluded. Individual OSM picnic-table nodes were grouped into five recognisable visitor locations rather than published as duplicate generic cards. Standalone attraction audit added 2026-08-08. These regional destinations are outside the active town boundary, appear only on Home discovery, and do not alter the town tourist rating.

Broad visitor-attraction editorial discovery pass 2026-08-13: expanded See discovery beyond historic records using a local OSM extract. Automatically discovered additions remain below Recommended until source-backed editorial review.

touristAppeal.label: Destination draw
touristAppeal.summary: Peterborough earns three stars for a nationally important cathedral, exceptional Bronze Age archaeology at Flag Fen, a strong city museum and a second day of green-space, railway and outdoor options at Ferry Meadows and Railworld.

townGuide.headline: A monumental cathedral, Bronze Age fen and easy waterside escapes
townGuide.intro: Peterborough pairs a vast Norman cathedral with Roman and local history at the city museum. Flag Fen carries the story into a Bronze Age landscape, while Ferry Meadows adds lakes, wildlife and easy waterside paths.
perfectFor: Families mixing history with Ferry Meadows
Visitors following Roman and Bronze Age stories

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Cathedral, museum and Cathedral Square
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Begin at the Cathedral while the precinct is quiet, cross to the museum for the wider city story, then use Cathedral Square for lunch before choosing Railworld or a drive to Flag Fen.

townGuide.suggestedTime: A full day; two days with Flag Fen and Ferry Meadows
townGuide.visitorMood: For heavyweight history, archaeology and easy green escapes in one short break.

visitorHighlights.name: Peterborough Cathedral
visitorHighlights.reason: Step beneath one of Europe’s great Norman interiors, look up at the rare painted wooden ceiling and find Katharine of Aragon’s tomb behind an unmistakable three-arched west front.

attractionGuide.toilets: Public toilets are available just outside the South Transept doors; ask a cathedral steward for directions.

thingsToDo.name: The Norman nave and painted ceiling
thingsToDo.summary: Walk the great Romanesque nave and look up at the rare painted wooden ceiling dating from around 1230.

thingsToDo.name: Katharine of Aragon's tomb
thingsToDo.summary: Find the Tudor queen's burial place and the former resting place of Mary, Queen of Scots.

thingsToDo.name: The New Building fan vaulting
thingsToDo.summary: Step into the late-medieval eastern extension for some of the cathedral's finest fan vaulting.

thingsToDo.name: The Hedda Stone
thingsToDo.summary: See the carved early medieval stone that survives from the cathedral's Saxon predecessor.

thingsToDo.name: A cathedral tour
thingsToDo.summary: Choose the one-hour ground-level Highlights Tour or, when available, the longer Upper Levels and Tower Tour.

visitorHighlights.name: Flag Fen Archaeology Park
visitorHighlights.reason: Walk beside the remains of a 3,500-year-old timber causeway and platform, then see preserved Bronze Age wood and Must Farm log boats in the landscape where they were found.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Seasonal opening; check the current calendar.

visitorHighlights.name: Ferry Meadows and Nene Park
visitorHighlights.reason: Trade city streets for lakes, meadows and woodland with easy waterside paths, wildlife, cycle routes, play areas and outdoor activities less than three miles from the centre.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Pedestrian and cycle access at all times; seasonal vehicle gates.

visitorHighlights.name: Peterborough Museum and Art Gallery
visitorHighlights.reason: Meet the city through Roman finds, archaeology, local social history and changing art displays inside a handsome Georgian building close to Cathedral Square.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free except selected exhibitions and events.

visitorHighlights.name: Longthorpe Tower
visitorHighlights.reason: A modest medieval tower hides one of England’s most remarkable surviving schemes of 14th-century domestic wall painting, best understood on a guided visit.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Seasonal guided opening on selected weekends; pre-book.
visitorHighlights.admission: Adult £5; child £3; concession £4; EH members free.

visitorHighlights.name: Railworld Wildlife Haven
visitorHighlights.reason: A volunteer-built mix of railway exhibits, model engineering and an unexpectedly leafy wildlife haven beside the main line gives families an eccentric, hands-on stop.

visitorHighlights.name: Peterborough Lido
visitorHighlights.reason: Swim outdoors beneath the diving stages of a handsome 1930s lido, a rare city-centre summer experience beside the river and embankment.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Seasonal sessions; check the current timetable.

visitorHighlights.name: New Theatre Peterborough
visitorHighlights.reason: Catch touring musicals, comedy, drama and family productions in Peterborough’s handsome refurbished art-deco theatre on Broadway.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Opens for performances; bars normally open 60 minutes before the show.

visitorHighlights.name: Key Theatre
visitorHighlights.reason: Pair a play, concert or comedy performance with a riverside walk at this intimate theatre on the Embankment.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Opens for performances and advertised events.

visitorHighlights.name: Peterborough Guildhall and Cathedral Square
visitorHighlights.reason: Pause beneath the open arches of the 1671 Guildhall and take in Cathedral Square, the natural hinge between the Cathedral, St John’s Church and the city centre.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Exterior viewable at all times; interior access is limited to special events.

visitorHighlights.name: Central Park
visitorHighlights.reason: A Green Flag park with formal gardens, mature trees, aviary and play space offers a gentle local pause north of the city centre.

visitorHighlights.name: Bishop's Gardens
visitorHighlights.reason: Slip behind the Cathedral precinct for a quiet green pause among lawns, mature trees and community garden planting close to the city centre.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Public outdoor garden; visit in daylight.

visitorHighlights.reason: Metal is a mapped arts centre within the active Peterborough visitor boundary and adds entertainment or culture to the town visit.
visitorHighlights.timeToSpend: Allow 1-3 hours, depending on the programme
